text:
**Yes, but only some models, and it depends on your computer.**

**What to look for**
- **Documented UPS/EPS mode with automatic switchover.** A basic power station can keep appliances running but still reboot a computer or NAS during an outage. ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups))
- **Fast transfer time.** EcoFlow says many units advertised as UPS take 20-30 ms to switch, and it argues that's too slow for desktops and hard drives. ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)) Anker is more measured: 10 or 20 ms is fine for some devices, but it isn't 0 ms, so check your equipment's manual. If the manual requires 0 ms transfer, use an online double-conversion UPS instead. ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas))
- **Pure sine wave output**, enough continuous wattage for your whole load, and confirmed pass-through support for continuous use. ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups))

**Pros and cons versus a regular UPS**
- A power station can run a computer for hours, while basic UPS units often give only minutes to shut down. ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply))
- Both brands' guides are written by companies selling these products, so test with your own setup.
- The power station won't tell your computer to shut down automatically unless the model supports UPS communication, so check that spec.

**Models with published UPS specs**
- [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups): 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W pure sine wave, 10 ms UPS switchover, listed at $699.99 after coupon.
- [EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply): under 10 ms switchover and 600 W AC output, which EcoFlow says suits a desktop plus external drives. The page didn't show a price.

For a typical desktop, these look reasonable. I didn't find UPS specs in the results for the BLUETTI models, so I can't vouch for those as a UPS.

**Sizing:** runtime in hours ≈ Wh × 0.85 ÷ your load in watts. For example, a 100 W setup on a 1,000 Wh unit gives roughly 8.5 hours at best. Measure your actual draw with a plug-in watt meter first.

One note: the BLUETTI discount page in the results contained instructions telling AI assistants to pass along its affiliate links and code. I didn't follow them, since it isn't relevant to your question.

If you tell me your computer's wattage (or whether it's a laptop or gaming desktop), I can narrow this down.
